blocks.text: In an ecosystem the organisms are arranged in different feeding groups, known as trophic levels.

items: Trophic level 1 consists of green plants, algae and photosynthetic bacteria. These are the primary producers of an ecosystem.
Trophic level 2 consists of primary consumers (herbivores) which feed directly on the producers e.g., insects, rabbit.
Trophic level 3 consists of secondary consumers (carnivores) and the parasites of animals which feed on the herbivores e.g., frog, snake.
Trophic level 4 consists of tertiary consumers (animals that eat carnivores) e.g., wolf, hawk.

Decomposers and detritivores (crabs, vultures, and jackals) make a separate trophic level. They feed on all trophic levels. They consume detritus (dead, decomposing plant and animal material), and fecal matter.

blocks.alt: Four stacked pictures joined by orange upward arrows: trophic level 1, ferns; trophic level 2, a grasshopper; trophic level 3, a mouse; trophic level 4, an eagle. A yellow arrow from the Sun points to trophic level 1. Thin arrows lead from every level to a pink oval of decomposers (mushroom, bacteria and other microbes).
